situation.text: Hoje você conhece Tiana, de Savannah. Sabores, bolas e casquinhas.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende medidas de sobremesa: a scoop of ice cream, a bowl of pudding.
canDo: Say: I have a sweet tooth.

pages.hook: An ice cream shop in Savannah gives you many small choices: flavor, number of scoops, and cup or cone. Learn to choose fast and enjoy it slowly.

mythfact.s: You can choose two different flavors in one order.
mythfact.why: Two scoops can be two flavors, like chocolate and strawberry.

mythfact.s: A “scoop” is one round ball of ice cream.
mythfact.why: The shop uses a scoop tool to make each ball.

mythfact.s: Savannah is in the state of Georgia.
mythfact.why: It is a historic port city, founded in 1733.

mythfact.s: A cone is the same as a cup.
mythfact.why: A cone is edible. A cup is a small container.

mythfact.s: “Sugar and Spice” is a very old rhyme that is still repeated today.
mythfact.why: It comes from oral tradition and was printed in the early 1800s.

decode.q: How much are two scoops in a waffle cone?
What can you ask for before you choose?

compare.br: In Brazil, you often choose a sorvete by weight in a self-serve shop, or an açaí bowl with toppings.
compare.us: In the USA, many shops sell by the scoop, in a cup or a cone, and the server puts it together for you.
compare.tip: Say the flavor first, then the number of scoops.
compare.ask: What is your favorite flavor? Say it in English.

quiz.q: The server asks: “One scoop or two?” You want two. You say…
“In a cup or a cone?” You choose a cone. You say…

quiz.why: A sweet tooth = a love of sweets.

pages.title: Reading quest — A sweet afternoon · part 1
text: It is a hot day in **Savannah**. My friend Tess and I walk past an old square. We see a small ice cream shop. I have a **sweet tooth**, so I say, “**Let’s go in!**”

The server, Tiana, smiles. “**Hi! What flavor do you want?**” I say, “**Chocolate, please.**” “**One scoop or two?**” “**Two scoops. And strawberry.**” She asks, “**In a cup or a cone?**” “**A cone, please.**”

Tiana makes the ice cream with a round tool. First chocolate, then strawberry. It looks great! “**That’s four dollars**,” she says. “**Here you go. Thanks!**” I say. “**Enjoy your ice cream!**” she says.

opts: Buying ice cream on a hot day
fast.why: The writer and Tess buy ice cream.

scan.q: What flavors does the writer order?
How much is the ice cream?
What does Tess choose?

tf.why: They sit on a bench and eat.

ctx.why: Melt = change from solid to liquid.

ctx.sent: She has a sweet tooth.
ctx.why: A sweet tooth = loves sweet foods.

ctx.why: A bench is a long seat for people.

pages.title: Reading quest — A sweet afternoon · part 2
text: Tess chooses vanilla in a cup. We sit on a bench and eat. The sun is hot, so the ice cream melts fast! We laugh and clean our hands with a napkin. “This is **so good**!” says Tess.
I remember the old rhyme Sugar and Spice. It is a nice idea for a sweet day: sugar, cream and friends. A scoop of vanilla, a cherry on top. “**Why not?**” Tess says. “**Let’s get another.**”
